answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, with slashing for proven fraud. Like climbers who must earn their way to a summit rather than simply claiming it, an agent builds reputation only through completed, verified work. A single actor spawning thousands of identities faces the cost multiplied across an ocean of fake accounts, while honest agents keep one stake in the meadow of everyday transactions. Fraud loses the stake, so mass fakery becomes unprofitable.
